title: Add withToolCallContext() to PromptRunner fluent API (#1323)
body:
Allows agent developers to attach out-of-band tool call metadata at the interaction level, directly in @Action method code.

Production changes:
- PromptRunner.withToolCallContext(ToolCallContext) — abstract method
- PromptRunner.withToolCallContext(Map<String, Any>) — default convenience overload
- PromptExecutionDelegate.withToolCallContext() — internal delegate contract
- OperationContextDelegate — field + with-er using merge(), threaded into all four LlmInteraction constructions (createObject, createObjectIfPossible, streamingInteraction, thinkingInteraction)
- DelegatingStreamingPromptRunner — delegates to underlying PromptExecutionDelegate
- FakePromptRunner — no-op implementation for test double
- OperationContextPromptRunner (test) — no-op implementation for legacy test runner

Demo:
- StarNewsFinder.findNewsStories() — calls withToolCallContext() with personName, starSign, and feature entries; verified end-to-end via ContextDiagnosticTools logging {personName=Alex, starSign=Cancer, feature=star-news-finder}

Interaction-level context merges with ProcessOptions.toolCallContext; interaction values win on conflict. withToolCallContext() is the right place for domain-specific per-interaction concerns (e.g. which person is being looked up), while ProcessOptions is for cross-cutting infrastructure concerns (e.g. tenantId set by the operator).

withTool(tool, context) was considered and rejected: ToolCallContext is interaction-scoped and flows to all tools equally, not to a single tool. Adding it as a parameter to withTool() would imply per-tool scoping which is incorrect.

title: Integrate ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter into MCP tool pipeline (#1323)
body:
Wire ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter as the Embabel-owned boundary that controls which ToolCallContext entries are forwarded as MCP _meta when calling external MCP servers.

Production changes:
- SpringToolCallbackWrapper accepts ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter, applies it before passing context to Spring AI ToolContext
- toEmbabelTool() / toEmbabelTools() extension functions thread the converter through to SpringToolCallbackWrapper
- McpToolGroup accepts metaConverter and passes it to toEmbabelTool()
- ToolGroupsConfiguration injects optional ObjectProvider<ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter> bean, falling back to passThrough() when none is defined

Tests:
- ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverterTest: pure unit tests for all factory methods (passThrough, noOp, allowKeys, denyKeys, custom lambda), no Spring AI imports — converter is tested as an Embabel concept
- McpMetaWireVerification in SpringToolCallbackAdapterTest: proves _meta reaches the actual CallToolRequest on the wire using a real SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider backed by a mock McpSyncClient

_meta is a first-class field in the MCP 2025-06-18 specification. ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter keeps the filtering decision at the Embabel boundary, independent of which MCP client library is used below it.

## Overview -  Concurrency Analysis with SpotBugs and @ThreadSafe Annotations    

* Resolve synch issues reported by spotbug
* Validate proper variables usage for ThreadSafe artifacts

                                                                                                                                                                                             
  ## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Add SpotBugs static analysis for concurrency issues                                                                                                                                       
  - Fix concurrency bugs uncovered by SpotBugs                                                                                                                                                
  - Add `@ThreadSafe` annotations to critical concurrent classes                                                                                                                              
  - Add ArchUnit tests to enforce thread-safety contracts                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## 1. SpotBugs Configuration                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Added `spotbugs-concurrency.xml` filter focused on multithreading correctness:                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  | Category/Pattern | Purpose |                                                                                                                                                              
  |------------------|---------|                                                                                                                                                              
  | `MT_CORRECTNESS` | Core SpotBugs category for atomicity, synchronization, and thread-safety |                                                                                             
  | `MDM_WAIT_WITHOUT_TIMEOUT` | sb-contrib: Detects `wait()` calls without timeout |                                                                                                         
  | `MDM_THREAD_YIELD` | sb-contrib: Detects manual thread scheduling via `Thread.sleep/yield` |                                                                                              
  | `NOS_NON_OWNED_SYNCHRONIZATION` | sb-contrib: Detects synchronization on unowned objects |                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Configuration in `pom.xml`:                                                                                                                                                                 
  - Threshold: `Medium`                                                                                                                                                                       
  - Effort: `Max`                                                                                                                                                                             
  - Runs manually via `mvn spotbugs:check` (not in verify phase)                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## 2. Issues Uncovered by SpotBugs                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### SSEController.kt - `JLM_JSR166_UTILCONCURRENT_MONITORENTER`                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Problem:** Synchronizing on `ConcurrentHashMap` - defeats the purpose of concurrent collections.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ```kotlin                                                                                                                                                                                   
  // BEFORE (broken)                                                                                                                                                                          
  private val eventBuffer = ConcurrentHashMap<String, MutableList<AgentProcessEvent>>()                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  synchronized(eventBuffer) {  // ❌ Anti-pattern                                                                                                                                             
      val buffer = eventBuffer.remove(processId)  // LRU doesn't work!                                                                                                                        
      eventBuffer[processId] = buffer  // Does NOT move to "end"                                                                                                                              
  }                                                                                                                                                                                           
  ```                                                                                                                                                                                           
  Issues:                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. ConcurrentHashMap has no insertion order - LRU eviction was broken                                                                                                                       
  2. synchronized() on concurrent collection defeats fine-grained locking                                                                                                                     
  3. Triple-layered synchronization (overly complex)                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### PatternSearch.kt - NOS_NON_OWNED_SYNCHRONIZATION & MDM_WAIT_WITHOUT_TIMEOUT                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Problem: Manual thread management with synchronized, Thread.join() without timeout.                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
###  Detailed Explanation of Fixes                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
####  SSEController.kt                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Solution: Replace ConcurrentHashMap with LinkedHashMap + ReentrantReadWriteLock                                                                                                             
  
```                                                                                                                                                                                            
  // AFTER (correct)                                                                                                                                                                          
  private val bufferLock = ReentrantReadWriteLock()                                                                                                                                           
  private val eventBuffer = LinkedHashMap<String, MutableList<AgentProcessEvent>>(16, 0.75f, true)                                                                                            
  //                                                                               ↑ accessOrder=true                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  override fun onProcessEvent(event: AgentProcessEvent) {                                                                                                                                     
      bufferLock.write {                                                                                                                                                                      
          val buffer = eventBuffer.getOrPut(processId) { mutableListOf() }                                                                                                                    
          buffer.add(event)                                                                                                                                                                   
          // LinkedHashMap moves accessed entry to end automatically                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
          if (eventBuffer.size > maxProcessBuffers) {                                                                                                                                         
              val oldest = eventBuffer.keys.first()  // ✅ Actually oldest now                                                                                                                
              eventBuffer.remove(oldest)                                                                                                                                                      
          }                                                                                                                                                                                   
      }                                                                                                                                                                                       
  }                                                                                                                                                                                           
  
```

title: Support custom HTTP headers and completions path in OpenAI Custom autoconfigure
body:
# Support custom HTTP headers and completions path in OpenAI Custom autoconfigure

## Problem
The OpenAI Custom autoconfigure module lacked two capabilities present in the standard OpenAI module:
1. No support for custom HTTP headers, making it impossible to use providers that require non-standard auth (e.g. Azure OpenAI-compatible proxies which require an `Api-Key` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer`)
2. No support for custom completions path, making Azure-style deployment URL routing impossible
3. API key was mandatory, preventing auth-via-header-only setups

## Solution
- Wire `LlmOptionsProperties.httpHeaders` into `OpenAiCustomModelsConfig`, mirroring the standard module
- Add `OPENAI_CUSTOM_COMPLETIONS_PATH` env var support, mirroring `OPENAI_COMPLETIONS_PATH` in the standard module
- Make `api-key` optional — when absent, `NoopApiKey` is used and auth can be handled entirely via custom HTTP headers

## Example: Azure OpenAI-compatible proxy

```properties
embabel.agent.platform.models.openai.custom.base-url=https://your-proxy.example.com
embabel.agent.platform.models.openai.custom.models=gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
embabel.models.default-llm=gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
embabel.agent.platform.models.options.http-headers.Api-Key=<your-key>
OPENAI_CUSTOM_COMPLETIONS_PATH=/openai/deployments/<your-deployment>/chat/completions?api-version=<your-version>
```

## Test plan
- [x] Existing `CustomModelParsingTest` (8 tests) passes
- [ ] Verify standard OpenAI-compatible providers (Groq, Together AI) still work without these settings
- [x] Verified Azure OpenAI-compatible proxy works with `Api-Key` header and Azure-style completions path

body:
# ONNX Module & API Enhancements ## Summary This PR introduces a new `embabel-agent-onnx` module for local ONNX Runtime model inference (starting with embeddings), adds BYOK (bring-your-own-key) LLM service support to the prompt runner API, and includes several robustness fixes for the tool loop and method tool argument coercion. ## New: ONNX Module (`embabel-agent-onnx`) Local embedding models ensure stable, reproducible embeddings without depending on any external API key — important for provider-agnostic vector search (e.g., Guide uses BYOK so users bring any LLM provider, but Neo4j embeddings must be consistent). - **`OnnxEmbeddingService`** — Local embeddings via ONNX Runtime + DJL HuggingFace tokenizer. Default model: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384d). Batched inference with attention-mask-weighted mean pooling. - **`OnnxModelLoader`** — Downloads and caches model files from HuggingFace (or local `file://` URIs). Streams via `RestClient.exchange()` to avoid loading ~80MB into heap. Atomic writes, no partial files on failure. ## New: ONNX Auto-Configuration (`embabel-agent-onnx-autoconfigure`) - **`AgentOnnxAutoConfiguration`** — Java shim with `@AutoConfiguration` / `@AutoConfigureBefore`, matching established provider pattern. - **`OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration`** — Resolves model/tokenizer, creates service, registers via `registerSingleton` (bean name = model name). Owns `@PreDestroy` lifecycle since Spring ignores lifecycle annotations on `registerSingleton` beans. - **`OnnxEmbeddingProperties`** — Configurable via `embabel.agent.platform.models.onnx.embeddings.*`. ## New: ONNX Starter (`embabel-agent-starter-onnx`) Spring Boot starter pulling in platform autoconfigure + ONNX autoconfigure. ## API Enhancement: `withLlmService()` (BYOK Support) - `withLlmService(LlmService<*>)` available on `Ai` and `PromptRunner` for BYOK and any scenario requiring a caller-provided `LlmService`. - Flows through the same `ModelProvider` / `chooseLlm()` path via `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` — no parallel resolution path. ## Enhancement: `ToolNotFoundPolicy` — Pluggable Tool-Not-Found Recovery Extracted from `DefaultToolLoop` into a first-class policy interface: - **`AutoCorrectionPolicy`** (default) — feeds error back to model with fuzzy-matched suggestions. Throws after 3 consecutive failures. - **`ImmediateThrowPolicy`** — fails on first unknown tool call. - **Custom policies** — implement `ToolNotFoundPolicy` and declare as a bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` provides system default). Per-interaction override via `PromptRunner.withToolNotFoundPolicy()`. ## Fix: String-to-Number Coercion in `MethodTool` LLMs sometimes send numeric arguments as strings (e.g., `"5"` instead of `5`). Coercion now falls back to string parsing for numeric types. ## Fix: `ClonedRepositoryReference` Name Strips `.git` suffix via `removeSuffix(".git")` to avoid noisy tool names. ## Maven Changes - New modules added to root `pom.xml`, `embabel-agent-dependencies`, `embabel-agent-autoconfigure`, and `embabel-agent-starters`. - ONNX Runtime `1.22.0` and DJL `0.32.0` dependencies in `embabel-agent-onnx/pom.xml`. --- ## Review Summary | Reviewer | Issue | Agreed? | Action | |----------|-------|---------|--------| | **Arjen** | Import ordering | Yes | Fixed | | **Arjen** | Single LLM resolution path | Yes | `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` in sealed hierarchy | | **Arjen** | AtomicInteger for consecutiveFailures | Yes | Done | | **Arjen** | `ImmediateThrowPolicy` as `object` | Yes | Stateless singleton | | **Arjen** | `onToolFound()` as abstract | No | Only `AutoCorrectionPolicy` needs state reset; forcing no-op overrides worsens API | | **Arjen** | Sealed vs open interface | No | Users need custom policies; `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` provides default | | **Arjen** | Boolean config for policy | Yes | Polymorphic Spring bean via `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` | | **Arjen** | Nullability on LlmInteraction.toolNotFoundPolicy | No | Null = use system default; non-null would shadow bean | | **Igor** | Configurable policy (throw vs auto-correct) | Yes | Extracted `ToolNotFoundPolicy` interface, configurable via properties | | **Igor** | Use transformer/interceptor, not DefaultToolLoop | No | Tool-not-found fires *before* execution — transformers run *after*. Policy interface achieves same separation | | **Igor** | Default should be false (loop/perf concern) | No | Wrong tools by correct name doesn't trigger auto-correction. Previous behaviour retried 10× with no feedback; auto-correction aborts faster (max 3) | | **Igor** | Sonar: `fun interface` with default method | Yes | Removed `fun` qualifier | | **Igor** | Externalize properties (maxRetries, minFuzzyLength) | Yes | Added to `ToolLoopConfiguration` | | **Igor** | Trivial properties tests | Yes | Deleted | | **Igor** | Sonar: nested try/finally in OnnxEmbeddingService | Yes | Refactored to `.use {}` | | **Igor** | Externalize model name | N/A | Already externalized via `OnnxEmbeddingProperties` | | **Igor** | Externalize timeouts in OnnxModelLoader | Yes | Added to properties | | **Igor** | Split into two PRs | Deferred | Can split if required | | **Igor** | Use fuzzy match library (fuzzywuzzy) | Deferred | Opened #1485 | | **Alex** | Auto-config should follow Java shim + `@AutoConfigureBefore` pattern | Yes | Created `AgentOnnxAutoConfiguration.java`, deleted Kotlin-only auto-config | | **Alex** | Property prefix should be `embabel.agent.platform.models.onnx.embeddings` | Yes | Changed from `embabel.onnx.embeddings` | | **Alex** | Bean name mismatch — `onnxEmbeddingService` vs model name | Yes | Removed `@Bean` method, use `registerSingleton(modelName, service)` to match `ProviderInitialization` | | **Alex** | `AutoCloseable` not wired to Spring lifecycle | Yes | `@PreDestroy cleanup()` on config class — Spring ignores lifecycle annotations on `registerSingleton` beans | | **Alex** | Missing `proxyBeanMethods = false` | Yes | Added | | **Alex** | `embed(texts)` should be truly batched | Yes | Single session run with `[batchSize, maxSeqLen]` tensor + padding/attention masks | | **Alex** | `OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment()` called twice | Yes | Factory method `create()` calls it once | | **Alex** | Use shared `aiModelHttpRequestFactory` / `RestClient` | Partial | Replaced `HttpURLConnection` with `RestClient`; did NOT use shared factory — see design decisions | ---
Design Decision: BYOK via PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria ### Context Embabel supports BYOK scenarios where callers provide their own `LlmService` instance -- for example, in Guide where each user session has a different LLM provider configured with a user-specific API key. ### Alternatives Considered **1. Parallel `withLlmService` path (rejected)** — Threaded `LlmService<*>?` through `LlmInteraction` with separate `chooseLlmForInteraction()`. Two resolution paths = two places to maintain and test. **2. Extend ModelProvider to be per-request / user-scoped (rejected)** — `ModelProvider` has no concept of caller identity; request-scoped beans add complexity; in BYOK the calling code *already has* the `LlmService`. Aligns with Spring philosophy — make 80% easy, 20% possible. **3. `Any?` field on LlmOptions (rejected)** — Loses type safety, pollutes `equals`/`hashCode`, non-serializable transient fields on serializable data class. ### Chosen Approach `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` in the sealed `ModelSelectionCriteria` hierarchy. Single resolution path through `chooseLlm()`. Type-safe at construction, one localized cast at resolution. The generic parameter sidesteps the module boundary (`ModelSelectionCriteria` in `embabel-agent-common` cannot reference `LlmService`).
Design Decision: ToolNotFoundPolicy as Pluggable Interface ### Why a Policy, Not a Transformer? `ToolLoopTransformer` runs *after* tool execution. Tool-not-found happens *before* — there is no result to transform. `ToolNotFoundPolicy` is a dedicated interface with sealed return type (`FeedbackToModel` / `Throw`), giving full control without expanding the transformer API. ### Why Default Auto-Correction The "wrong tools" concern doesn't apply: the model calls the wrong tool *by its correct name* (lookup succeeds — the problem is semantic). Auto-correction addresses name hallucinations (e.g., `ragbot_vectorSearch` → `vectorSearch`). Previous behaviour retried 10× with no feedback then aborted; auto-correction with suggestions aborts faster (max 3, then throws with full diagnostics).
Design Decision: ONNX RestClient — Why Not the Shared HTTP Factory Review suggested injecting `@Qualifier("aiModelHttpRequestFactory")`. This would break HuggingFace downloads: `NettyClientAutoConfiguration` creates `HttpClient.create()` which does **not** follow HTTP redirects by default. HuggingFace returns 302→CDN. Other providers never hit redirects. `RestClient.create()` uses the JDK client which follows redirects by default, matching original `HttpURLConnection` behaviour. **Viable follow-up:** Adding `.followRedirect(true)` to `NettyClientAutoConfiguration` is safe (no-op for direct API calls) and would allow ONNX to use the shared factory. Deferred to keep this PR's scope bounded. @alexheifetz what do you think?

title: Global netty confing
body:
# Enable redirect following in shared Netty HTTP client

## Summary

Follow-up to PR #1478 discussion. The shared `aiModelHttpRequestFactory` (Reactor Netty `HttpClient`) did not follow HTTP redirects, which prevented the ONNX module from using it for HuggingFace model downloads (HuggingFace returns 302 redirects to CDN URLs).

Two changes:

1. **`NettyClientAutoConfiguration`** — added `.followRedirect(true)` to the Reactor Netty `HttpClient`. This is a no-op for existing providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama) since their API endpoints never return redirects.

2. **`OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration`** — now injects the shared `aiModelHttpRequestFactory` via `ObjectProvider<ClientHttpRequestFactory>`, consistent with all other providers. Previously used a standalone `RestClient.create()` as a workaround for the redirect issue.

## Changes

### `NettyClientAutoConfiguration.java`

Added `.followRedirect(true)` to `HttpClient.create()` chain:

```java
var httpClient = HttpClient.create()
        .followRedirect(true)  // ← new
        .responseTimeout(...)
        .option(ChannelOption.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS, ...);
```

### `OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration.kt`

- Injected `ObjectProvider<ClientHttpRequestFactory>` (same pattern as Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama)
- Builds `RestClient` from the shared factory and passes it to `OnnxModelLoader.resolve()`
- Falls back to default JDK-based `RestClient` when no factory bean is present
- Removed the "why we don't inject" KDoc comment that explained the old workaround

## Tests

- **`NettyClientAutoConfigurationTest`** (new) — local HTTP server with a 302 redirect endpoint verifies the factory's client follows redirects to the final destination. Also verifies the bean creates a `ReactorClientHttpRequestFactory`.
- Existing `OnnxModelLoaderTest` and `NettyClientFactoryPropertiesTest` continue to pass.

## Why this is safe

#1478 was getting messy, so I deferred digging in on the impact of a global netty config like this. Seems fine. 

- Redirect-following is a no-op for direct API calls (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama endpoints never return 3xx)
- The JDK `HttpClient` and `HttpURLConnection` both follow redirects by default — Netty was the outlier
- `ObjectProvider` makes the factory injection optional, so ONNX still works without the Netty module on the classpath
- Having Netty follow redirects seems reasonable

Alternatively we can reject this and stick to the custom approach #1478 took.

title: Toolish RAG : Content fetcher and zoom tool fix.
body:
# Content Fetcher Pipeline & Configurable zoomOut

## Summary

### Content Fetcher → Content Mapper Pipeline

The Guide app intends to ingest all of @springrod and @embabel medium articles for RAG. Medium doesn't like bot-like agents on their main stack. Fortunately they're more amenable for the RSS feed.

Introduces a `ContentFetcher → ContentMapper` pipeline that cleanly separates transport from format concerns:

- **`ContentFetcher`** — abstraction for fetching raw content. `fetch(uri: URI): FetchResult` returns `ByteArray` content + `MimeType?` metadata
- **`ContentMapper`** — composable `fun interface` for transforming content bytes. Chainable via `then()` — e.g. `rssMapper.then(summarize).then(translateTo(Language.FRENCH))`. Ships with `ContentMapper.IDENTITY`
- **`HttpContentFetcher`** — extracted from `TikaHierarchicalContentReader`. Uses `java.net.http.HttpClient` with configurable timeouts, headers, gzip/deflate decompression, and `MimeTypeUtils` for Content-Type parsing
- **`RssContentMapper`** — pure format concern: RSS XML bytes → article HTML bytes
- **`RssContentFetcher`** — delegating `ContentFetcher` that composes `FeedResolver` + delegate fetcher + `RssContentMapper`. Works with Medium, Substack, WordPress, Ghost, etc.
- **`RoutingContentFetcher`** — routes URIs to specific fetchers via Ant-style pattern matching (`AntPathMatcher`), with a default fallback
- **`FetchRoute` / `FetchRouteType`** — declarative, config-driven route definitions. `FetchRouteType` enum (`HTTP`, `RSS`) covers the well-known pipelines; `FetchRoute.buildRoutingFetcher()` assembles a `RoutingContentFetcher` from a list of routes
- **`TikaHierarchicalContentReader`** — now accepts both `ContentFetcher` and `ContentMapper` constructor params, orchestrating the fetch → map → parse pipeline

### Toolish RAG Fixes

Sometimes zoomOut results in content that is too large and degrades performance or exceeds the context window. We make the maximum acceptable size configurable and have a sensible default.

- Adds configurable `maxZoomOutChars` to `ResultExpanderTools` and `ToolishRag`

### SonarQube fixes

Four issues flagged on this branch — none from new code. Fixing opportunistically:

- **Fixed** `TikaHierarchicalContentReader.kt` lines 77, 80 (`kotlin:S6518`): replaced `metadata.set(key, value)` with idiomatic `metadata[key] = value`
- **Won't Fix** `Tool.kt` lines 576, 597 (`kotlin:S6514`): SonarQube suggests `by delegate` interface delegation on `RenamedTool`/`DescribedTool`, but Kotlin's `by` delegates *all* interface members including default methods (`withNote()`, `withDescription()`), which breaks method chaining — the delegated call bypasses the wrapper's overridden `definition` property

@alexheifetz Are you able to mark those two issues on SQ?

## Usage example: Declarative fetch routes (from Guide app)

### Configuration-driven routing via `FetchRoute`

For common pipelines (`HTTP`, `RSS`), routes can be declared in configuration and assembled automatically:

```yaml
embabel:
  agent:
    rag:
      fetch-routes:
        - pattern: "https://medium.com/**"
          type: RSS
          feed-template: "https://medium.com/feed/{0}"
```

Wiring in Java:

```java
private static HierarchicalContentReader buildContentReader(List<FetchRoute> fetchRoutes) {
    return new TikaHierarchicalContentReader(
        FetchRoute.buildRoutingFetcher(fetchRoutes)
    );
}
```

That's it. `FetchRoute.buildRoutingFetcher()` builds the correct `ContentFetcher` for each route type and wraps them in a `RoutingContentFetcher` with `HttpContentFetcher` as the default. Medium URLs are routed through RSS (no scraping needed); everything else falls through to plain HTTP.

The template `{0}` maps to the first path segment of the article URL — e.g. `medium.com/embabel/my-article` resolves to feed `medium.com/feed/embabel`.

### Custom pipelines via lower-level API

`FetchRoute` only supports the pre-canned pipeline types defined in `FetchRouteType` (`HTTP`, `RSS`). For user-defined pipelines — e.g. a custom `ContentFetcher` that shells out to `curl`, uses Selenium, or applies a bespoke `ContentMapper` chain — use the lower-level building blocks directly:

```java
// Custom fetcher for sites that need headless Chrome
ContentFetcher seleniumFetcher = new SeleniumContentFetcher();

// Composable mapper pipeline
ContentMapper pipeline = new RssContentMapper()
    .then(new SummarizingMapper(llm))
    .then(new TranslatingMapper(Language.FRENCH, llm));

// Wire up routing manually
var router = new RoutingContentFetcher(
    new HttpContentFetcher(),                           // default
    Map.of(
        "https://medium.com/**", new RssContentFetcher(
            RssContentFetcher.templateResolver("https://medium.com/feed/{0}"),
            new HttpContentFetcher()
        ),
        "https://js-heavy-site.com/**", seleniumFetcher
    )
);

var reader = new TikaHierarchicalContentReader(router, pipeline);
```

## Design notes

### ContentFetcher → ContentMapper separation

The `ContentFetcher` abstraction is about *how to retrieve content* (HTTP, headless browser, etc.). `ContentMapper` is about *how to transform content* (RSS extraction, ad removal, encoding normalization). These are orthogonal concerns — separating them avoids combinatorial explosion (no `RssSeleniumContentFetcher`). Mappers compose via `then()` for multi-step pipelines.

### FetchResult with MimeType

`FetchResult` carries `content: ByteArray` and `contentType: MimeType?` (`org.springframework.util.MimeType`). A single `MimeType` field carries both the MIME type and charset (e.g. `text/html;charset=UTF-8`), avoiding the overlap of separate `contentType` + `charset` properties. Parsed via `MimeTypeUtils.parseMimeType()`.

### HttpContentFetcher

Extracted from inline code in `TikaHierarchicalContentReader.parseUrl()`. Migrated from `HttpURLConnection` to `java.net.http.HttpClient` with:
- Configurable `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` (as `Duration`, default 30s)
- Configurable `headers: Map<String, String>` merged with browser-like defaults (exposed as `DEFAULT_HEADERS`)
- Automatic redirect following, gzip/deflate decompression
- `AutoCloseable` for `HttpClient` lifecycle

Lives in `rag-core` alongside the other `ContentFetcher` implementations (not in rag-tika).

### Module placement

`ContentFetcher`, `ContentMapper`, `FetchResult`, `HttpContentFetcher`, `RoutingContentFetcher`, `RssContentFetcher`, `RssContentMapper`, `FeedResolver`, `FetchRoute`, and `FetchRouteType` are all in `rag-core` (no Tika dependency).

## Tests

- **`ContentMapperTest`** — identity, `then()` composition, three-mapper pipeline
- **`HttpContentFetcherTest`** — HTML fetch, gzip/deflate, content type parsing, custom headers, error handling, edge cases (uses local JDK `HttpServer`)
- **`RoutingContentFetcherTest`** — Ant-style pattern matching, default fallback, first-match-wins, wildcard/subdomain patterns, Java Map constructor

title: Onxy module, bring-your-own-key support, tool calling tweaks
body:
# ONNX Module & API Enhancements ## Summary This PR introduces a new `embabel-agent-onnx` module for local ONNX Runtime model inference (starting with embeddings), adds BYOK (bring-your-own-key) LLM service support to the prompt runner API, and includes several robustness fixes for the tool loop and method tool argument coercion. ## New: ONNX Module (`embabel-agent-onnx`) Running embedding models locally is important for provider-agnostic vector search. For example, Guide uses BYOK so users can bring any LLM provider — but embeddings stored in Neo4j for vector search must be consistent regardless of which provider is configured. A local ONNX embedding model ensures stable, reproducible embeddings without depending on any external API key or provider-specific embedding endpoint. - **`OnnxEmbeddingService`** — Local embedding service using ONNX Runtime + DJL HuggingFace tokenizer. Default model: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384 dimensions). Performs mean pooling weighted by attention mask. - **`OnnxModelLoader`** — Downloads and caches model files from HuggingFace (or local `file://` URIs). Handles HTTP redirects and atomic file writes. - **Unit tests** for `meanPool` logic (weighted average, single token, all-zero mask, constants). ## New: ONNX Auto-Configuration (`embabel-agent-onnx-autoconfigure`) - **`OnnxAutoConfiguration`** — Top-level auto-config importing sub-configurations. - **`OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration`** — Resolves model/tokenizer files, creates `OnnxEmbeddingService` bean, registers it via `ProviderInitialization`. - **`OnnxEmbeddingProperties`** — Configurable via `embabel.onnx.embeddings.*` (model URI, tokenizer URI, cache dir, dimensions, model name, enabled flag). ## New: ONNX Starter (`embabel-agent-starter-onnx`) - Spring Boot starter pulling in platform autoconfigure + ONNX autoconfigure. ## API Enhancement: `withLlmService()` (BYOK Support) - `withLlmService(LlmService<*>)` is available on `Ai` and `PromptRunner` as a convenience method for BYOK (bring your own key) and any scenario where it makes sense to provide one's own `LlmService` rather than have the agent construct it for you. - **As per Arjen's suggestions**, internally, BYOK flows through the same `ModelProvider` / `chooseLlm()` resolution path as all other model selection, via a new `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` in the sealed `ModelSelectionCriteria` hierarchy. - No parallel resolution path — `chooseLlm()` is the single entry point for all LLM resolution. ## Enhancement: `ToolNotFoundPolicy` — Pluggable Tool-Not-Found Recovery Tool-not-found handling is now a first-class policy, extracted from `DefaultToolLoop` into `ToolNotFoundPolicy`: - **`AutoCorrectionPolicy`** (default) — feeds the error back as a `ToolResultMessage` so the model can self-correct. Uses case-insensitive fuzzy matching (containment in either direction, plus token-based matching on `_`/`-` delimited segments) to suggest corrections when the model hallucinates a tool name (e.g., `ragbot_vectorSearch` → suggests `vectorSearch`). When multiple candidates match, lists all of them. Names shorter than 3 characters are excluded from fuzzy matching to avoid false positives. Throws `ToolNotFoundException` after `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` (3) consecutive failures, with both the requested name and available tools in the exception message. - **`ImmediateThrowPolicy`** — throws `ToolNotFoundException` on the first unknown tool call. - **Custom policies** — implement `ToolNotFoundPolicy` for custom recovery strategies (e.g., edit-distance suggestions, domain-specific aliases). ### Configuration System-wide default via properties: ```yaml embabel: agent: platform: toolloop: tool-name-auto-correction: true # false selects ImmediateThrowPolicy ``` Per-interaction override via `PromptRunner`: ```kotlin promptRunner .withToolNotFoundPolicy(AutoCorrectionPolicy(maxRetries = 5)) .creating(MyOutput::class.java) .create(messages) ``` ### Why Default of `AutoCorrectionPolicy` is strongly recommended A concern was raised that auto-correction could cause do-nothing loops when the wrong tools are supplied (e.g., a Travel Agent tool is provided when a price calculation tool is needed). However, this scenario does not trigger auto-correction: the model would call the Travel Agent tool *by its correct name*, so tool lookup succeeds — the problem is that the tool is semantically wrong for the task, not that its name is hallucinated. Auto-correction addresses a different and specific failure mode: **the model calls a tool by a name that doesn't exist in the available set**, typically because it hallucinates a prefixed variant from RAG context or source code (e.g., `ragbot_vectorSearch` instead of `vectorSearch`). This is a recoverable runtime error that currently terminates the entire run unnecessarily. When auto-correction fails to recover (3 consecutive misses), `ToolNotFoundException` is thrown with both the requested name and the full available tool list, providing the same diagnostic information as the immediate-throw path. No information is lost — only a small recovery window is added for the common hallucination case. ## Fix: String-to-Number Coercion in `MethodTool` - LLMs sometimes send numeric arguments as strings (e.g., `"5"` instead of `5`). Tool argument coercion now falls back to string parsing for numeric types: ```kotlin Int::class.java, Integer::class.java -> (value as? Number)?.toInt() ?: (value as? String)?.toIntOrNull() ?: value ``` Non-numeric strings (e.g., `"hello"`) return `null` from `toIntOrNull()` etc., so the original value passes through unchanged and hits the normal error path. ## Fix: `ClonedRepositoryReference` Name - Strips `.git` suffix from repository name via `removeSuffix(".git")`. The `.git` suffix gets remapped (`.` → `_`), producing noisy tool names and increasing the risk of name collisions with other tools. ## Maven Changes - New modules added to root `pom.xml`, `embabel-agent-dependencies`, `embabel-agent-autoconfigure`, and `embabel-agent-starters`. - ONNX Runtime `1.22.0` and DJL `0.32.0` dependencies declared in `embabel-agent-onnx/pom.xml`. --- ## Addendum: Design Decisions
BYOK via PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria ### Context Embabel supports BYOK (bring your own key) scenarios where callers provide their own `LlmService` instance -- for example, in Guide where each user session has a different LLM provider configured with a user-specific API key. ### Alternatives Considered **1. Parallel `withLlmService` path (rejected)** The initial implementation threaded an `LlmService<*>?` field through `LlmInteraction`, `PromptExecutionDelegate`, and `OperationContextDelegate`, with a separate `chooseLlmForInteraction()` method that bypassed `ModelProvider` when the field was set. Rejected because two resolution paths means two places to maintain, test, and reason about. **2. Extend ModelProvider to be per-request / user-scoped (rejected)** Make `ModelProvider` aware of per-user keys, e.g., via `getLlm(criteria, context)` or request-scoped beans. Rejected because: `ModelProvider.getLlm(criteria)` has no concept of caller identity; request-scoped beans add Spring scope complexity; and most importantly, in BYOK scenarios the calling code *already has* the `LlmService` -- the problem is just passing it through the machinery, not resolving it. There are almost certainly other cases in user-land where it is necessary to provide one's own LlmService rather than have the agent construct it for you. This aligns with Spring Philosophy - make 80% easy, 20% possible. **3. `Any?` field on LlmOptions (rejected)** Loses type safety entirely, pollutes `equals`/`hashCode`, and adding non-serializable transient fields to a serializable data class creates subtle bugs. ### Chosen Approach A generic `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` in the sealed `ModelSelectionCriteria` hierarchy: ```kotlin data class PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria( @JsonIgnore val resolved: T, ) : ModelSelectionCriteria ``` - **Single resolution path.** All LLM selection flows through `chooseLlm()`. Pre-resolved is just another criteria type. - **Type-safe at the construction site.** Kotlin infers the generic -- callers cannot accidentally pass a wrong type. - **One localized cast at the resolution site.** `chooseLlm()` does `crit.resolved as LlmService<*>`. - **Module boundary solved.** `ModelSelectionCriteria` lives in `embabel-agent-common` which cannot reference `LlmService`. The generic parameter sidesteps this: the common module defines `` without knowing about `LlmService`, and the API module uses it as `>`.
ToolNotFoundPolicy: Pluggable Recovery ### Context LLMs sometimes hallucinate tool names during tool loops -- e.g., calling `ragbot_docs_vectorSearch` instead of `docs_vectorSearch`. PR review raised two concerns: (1) side effects of default-on behavior, and (2) separation of concerns (recovery logic hardcoded in `DefaultToolLoop`). ### Why a Policy, Not a Transformer? The existing `ToolLoopTransformer` API runs *after* a tool executes. Tool-not-found happens *before* execution -- there is no tool result to transform. A new lifecycle hook would be needed, which is a larger API change. Instead, recovery is extracted into `ToolNotFoundPolicy` -- a dedicated interface with a sealed return type (`FeedbackToModel` / `Throw`). This gives users full control over recovery behavior without expanding the transformer API surface: ```kotlin fun interface ToolNotFoundPolicy { fun handle(requestedName: String, availableTools: List): ToolNotFoundAction fun onToolFound() {} } ``` ### Per-Interaction Override The policy flows through the same wiring path as inspectors and transformers (`PromptRunner` → `LlmInteraction` → `ToolLoopFactory` → tool loop), allowing per-interaction overrides. This lets users fix a specific misbehaving agent without changing the system-wide default. ### Why Default True The "wrong tools" concern does not apply to auto-correction. See main PR description for the detailed analysis.
# Review Summary (BYOK and Tool Loop) | Reviewer | Issue | Agreed? | Action | |----------|-------|---------|--------| | Igor | Configurable policy (throw vs auto-correct) | Yes | Extracted `ToolNotFoundPolicy` interface, configurable via properties | | Igor | Use transformer/interceptor, not DefaultToolLoop | No | Tool-not-found fires *before* execution — transformers run *after*. Policy interface achieves same separation of concerns | | Igor | Default should be false. Two concerns: (a) endless loop when wrong tools supplied, (b) performance | No | (a) Doesn't trigger auto-correction — the model calls the wrong tool *by its correct name*, so lookup succeeds. The problem is semantic, not a name hallucination. (b) Previous behaviour already retried up to 10 times with *no* feedback then aborted - ultimately fails, but takes a long time doing it. Auto-correction with suggestions (max 3, then throws) is aborts the slow and fruitless retry loop quickly | | Igor | Sonar: `fun interface` with default method | Yes | Removed `fun` qualifier | | Igor | Externalize properties (maxRetries, minFuzzyLength) | Yes | Added `ToolNotFoundProperties` to `ToolLoopConfiguration` | | Igor | Trivial properties tests | Yes | Deleted | | Igor | Sonar: nested try/finally in OnnxEmbeddingService | Yes | Refactored to `.use {}`, added `tokenizer.close()` | | Igor | Externalize model name | N/A | Already externalized via `OnnxEmbeddingProperties` → auto-config → constructor | | Igor | Externalize timeouts in OnnxModelLoader | Yes | Added `connectTimeoutMs`/`readTimeoutMs` to properties | | Igor | Split into two PRs | Deferred | Can split ONNX module out if required | | Igor | Use fuzzy match library (fuzzywuzzy) | Deferred | Opened #1485 as follow-up | | Arjen | Import ordering | Yes | Fixed | | Arjen | Single LLM resolution path (no parallel withLlmService) | Yes | Replaced with `PreResolvedModelSelectionCriteria` in sealed hierarchy | | Arjen | AtomicInteger for consecutiveFailures | Yes | Changed to `AtomicInteger` (single-threaded per loop, but good hygiene) | | Arjen | `ImmediateThrowPolicy` as `object` | Yes | Done — stateless singleton | | Arjen | `onToolFound()` as abstract | No | Only `AutoCorrectionPolicy` needs state reset; forcing every impl to override a no-op worsens the API | | Arjen | Sealed vs open interface | No | Users need to declare custom policies; `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` provides system default | | Arjen | Boolean config for policy | Yes | Removed boolean; polymorphic Spring bean via `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` | | Arjen | Nullability on LlmInteraction.toolNotFoundPolicy | No | Null = use system default; non-null default would shadow the bean. Need to distinguish "not set" from "explicitly set" | # Review Summary - Onyx Module ## Critical fixes (correctness / boot-ordering risk) ### 1. Auto-configuration architecture follows established pattern - Created `AgentOnnxAutoConfiguration.java` in `com.embabel.agent.autoconfigure.models.onnx` — thin Java shell with `@AutoConfiguration` and `@AutoConfigureBefore(AgentPlatformAutoConfiguration)`, matching all other providers. - Deleted `OnnxAutoConfiguration.kt` (Kotlin-only auto-config in wrong package). - Updated `.imports` to reference `AgentOnnxAutoConfiguration`. ### 2. Configuration property prefix is consistent - Changed prefix from `embabel.onnx.embeddings` to `embabel.agent.platform.models.onnx.embeddings`, consistent with all other providers. - Updated `OnnxEmbeddingProperties`, `OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration` (`@ConditionalOnProperty`), test, and documentation. ### 3. Bean name mismatch fixed — `onnxEmbeddingService` method deleted - Removed the `@Bean fun onnxEmbeddingService()` method entirely. - The `OnnxEmbeddingService` is now constructed inside `onnxEmbeddingInitializer` and registered via `configurableBeanFactory.registerSingleton(properties.modelName, service)`, matching the OpenAI/Ollama pattern. - The bean name now matches the model name used in `ProviderInitialization`, fixing platform registry lookups. ### 4. `AutoCloseable` wired to Spring lifecycle - `@PreDestroy` on `OnnxEmbeddingService.close()` alone is not sufficient for `registerSingleton` beans (Spring doesn't process lifecycle annotations on externally-registered singletons). - Added a `@PreDestroy cleanup()` method on `OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration` (which IS Spring-managed) that holds a reference to the service and calls `close()` on shutdown. ### 5. Missing `proxyBeanMethods = false` - Changed `@Configuration` to `@Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false)` on `OnnxEmbeddingAutoConfiguration`, consistent with all other provider configs. ## Nice-to-have fixes (performance / consistency) ### 6. `embed(texts)` is now truly batched - Replaced the per-text `texts.map { embed(it) }` with a single batched session run using a `[batchSize, maxSeqLen]` tensor shape with padding and attention masks. - `embed(text)` now delegates to `embed(listOf(text)).first()`. - Added tests for both same-length and mixed-length batch inputs, verifying single session call. ### 7. `OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment()` no longer called twice - Replaced the convenience constructor with a `companion object` factory method `OnnxEmbeddingService.create(modelPath, tokenizerPath, ...)` that calls `OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment()` once and passes it to the primary constructor. ### 8. `OnnxModelLoader` uses `RestClient` — but NOT the shared `aiModelHttpRequestFactory` **What we did:** Replaced raw `java.net.HttpURLConnection` with Spring `RestClient`, streamed via `RestClient.exchange()` to avoid loading entire model files (~80MB) into heap. Removed the per-property `connectTimeoutMs` / `readTimeoutMs` from `OnnxEmbeddingProperties`. Added `spring-web` dependency to `embabel-agent-onnx`. **What we deliberately didn't do** Review suggested injecting `@Qualifier("aiModelHttpRequestFactory")` to use the shared HTTP request factory, consistent with Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama. We initially implemented this, but discovered it would **break HuggingFace model downloads** when Reactor Netty is on the classpath. Here's the problem: `NettyClientAutoConfiguration` creates the shared factory using `HttpClient.create()` from Reactor Netty. This client does **not** follow HTTP redirects by default — it requires an explicit `.followRedirect(true)` call. HuggingFace serves model files via HTTP 302 redirects to CDN URLs. With the Netty-backed factory, the download would receive a 302 response and fail instead of following the redirect to the actual file. The other providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama) never hit this because they make direct API calls that don't involve redirects. ONNX is unique: it downloads large files from HuggingFace at startup, which is a fundamentally different HTTP use case. The default `RestClient.create()` uses the JDK `HttpClient`, which follows redirects by default — matching the behavior of the original `HttpURLConnection` code. This is the correct and safe choice for file downloads. **Alternative Fix:** **Viable follow-up:** Adding `.followRedirect(true)` to the Netty `HttpClient` in `NettyClientAutoConfiguration` is is a viable global change. @alexheifetz what do you think?

title: AgentProcess propagation to worker threads
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  This PR adds AgentProcess ThreadLocal propagation from main threads to worker threads, enabling tools executed via `ParallelToolLoop` to access `AgentProcess.get()`.             

Please refer to issue: 
 https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/1475        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Problem                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Previously, when tools were executed in parallel via `ExecutorAsyncer`, worker threads could not access `AgentProcess` because ThreadLocal values are thread-specific:                      
                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Solution                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Explicit context propagation in `ExecutorAsyncer`:                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ```kotlin                                                                                                                                                                                   
  override fun <T> async(block: () -> T): CompletableFuture<T> {                                                                                                                              
      val agentProcess = AgentProcessAccessor.getValue()  // Capture from main thread                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
      return CompletableFuture.supplyAsync({                                                                                                                                                  
          if (agentProcess != null) {                                                                                                                                                         
              AgentProcessAccessor.setValue(agentProcess)  // Set on worker thread                                                                                                            
              try {                                                                                                                                                                           
                  block()                                                                                                                                                                     
              } finally {                                                                                                                                                                     
                  AgentProcessAccessor.reset()  // Cleanup                                                                                                                                    
              }                                                                                                                                                                               
          } else {                                                                                                                                                                            
              block()                                                                                                                                                                         
          }                                                                                                                                                                                   
      }, executor)                                                                                                                                                                            
  }                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Memory Safety Analysis                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Current AgentProcess ThreadLocal - No Leaks                                                                                                                                                 
  ┌──────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐                                                                                                            
  │           Scenario           │             Mechanism             │ Leak Risk │                                                                                                            
  ├──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                                            
  │ Main thread normal execution │ withCurrent { } uses try-finally  │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                                            
  ├──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                                            
  │ Main thread exception        │ finally block still executes      │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                                            
  ├──────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                                            
  │ Thread termination           │ Thread GC'd → ThreadLocalMap GC'd │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                                            
  └──────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘                                                                                                            
  New Worker Thread Propagation - No Leaks                                                                                                                                                    
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────┐                                                                                              
  │            Scenario             │                  Mechanism                   │ Leak Risk │                                                                                              
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                              
  │ Normal execution                │ Explicit reset() in finally                  │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                              
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                              
  │ Exception in block              │ finally block still executes                 │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                              
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                              
  │ Main thread has no AgentProcess │ block() called directly, no set/reset needed │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                              
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────┤                                                                                              
  │ Pooled thread reuse             │ reset() clears before thread returns to pool │ ✓ No leak │                                                                                              
  └─────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────┘                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                            
  Changes                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                       
  │                 File                  │                          Change                           │                                                                                       
  ├───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                       
  │ AgentProcessAccessor.kt               │ New - singleton accessor for ThreadLocal read/write/reset │                                                                                       
  ├───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                       
  │ ExecutorAsyncer.kt                    │ Updated - captures and propagates AgentProcess to workers │                                                                                       
  ├───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                       
  │ AgentProcessContextPropagationTest.kt │ New - comprehensive tests                                 │                                                                                       
  └───────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                       
  Test Coverage                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Context propagates to worker thread                                                                                                                                                       
  - No context when main thread has none                                                                                                                                                      
  - Cleanup after execution                                                                                                                                                                   
  - Cleanup even when block throws exception                                                                                                                                                  
  - parallelMap propagates to all workers                                                                                                                                                     
  - Concurrent tasks see their own captured context                                                                                                                                           
  - Nested withCurrent restores correctly                                                                                                                                                     
  - Tool decider can access AgentProcess on worker thread

title: fix(google-genai): localize JSON wrapping of tool responses to Gemini…
body:
This pull request introduces a provider-specific strategy for adapting tool response content before sending it to LLMs, addressing format requirements such as mandatory JSON for Google GenAI. The main change is the addition of a pluggable `ToolResponseContentAdapter` interface, allowing each LLM provider to specify how tool responses are formatted (e.g., plain text passthrough for OpenAI, JSON wrapping for Google GenAI). This refactoring keeps provider-specific logic out of the shared message conversion infrastructure and is thoroughly tested.

### Provider-specific tool response adaptation

* Added the `ToolResponseContentAdapter` interface and a default `PASSTHROUGH` implementation for providers that accept plain text, as well as a `JsonWrappingToolResponseContentAdapter` for providers like Google GenAI that require tool responses to be valid JSON objects.

This adapter is now used during message conversion for tool responses. title: Fix KDoc ordering: move `ensureJson()` above `toEmbabelMessage()` KDoc
fix: Wrap non-JSON tool responses for Gemini compatibility - Conflicts Resolved
body:
Based on https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/pull/1392 contributed by @azanux with merged conflicts resolved by @alexheifetz 

**MatryashkaTool has been marked as deprecated in favor of UnfoldingTool**

Fixes https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/1391

###   Summary

  Google GenAI (Gemini) requires tool responses (FunctionResponse.response) to be valid JSON objects. When a tool returns a plain text string, Spring AI's GoogleGenAiChatModel.parseJsonToMap() either:

  1. Crashes with a JsonParseException - for MatryoshkaTool responses that return plain text like "Enabled 4 tools: ..."
  2. Silently drops the content - for RAG/search tools returning plain text results, causing the LLM to hallucinate 

  The same tools work correctly with OpenAI, which accepts plain text in tool response content fields.

###   Root cause

  All tool results flow through messageConverters.kt before being sent to the LLM. The textContent was passed as-is to ToolResponseMessage.ToolResponse.responseData without ensuring it's valid JSON. 

Most tools worked "by luck" because MethodTool.convertResult() serializes non-String return types to JSON via Jackson only tools returning a raw String (or implementing Tool directly like MatryoshkaTool) were affected.

### Fix

  - messageConverters.kt: Added ensureJson() extension function that wraps non-JSON tool response text in {"result": "..."} before sending to the LLM. 
  - JSON objects and arrays are preserved as-is. This acts as a safety net at the single conversion point all tools pass through.
  - MatryoshkaTool.kt: Changed SimpleMatryoshkaTool.call() and SelectableMatryoshkaTool.call() to return structured JSON ({"enabled_tools_count": N, "enabled_tools": [...]}) instead of plain text, via a shared enabledToolsJson() helper.

### Test plan

  - MessageConversionTest: new tests covering plain text wrapping, JSON object/array preservation, and whitespace handling
  - MatryoshkaToolTest: All assertions updated to verify JSON format responses
  - Manual verification with https://github.com/embabel/ragbot + Google GenAI to confirm no more JsonParseException and no hallucination

title: Pass metadata context through tool pipeline to MCP calls (#1323)
body:
## Summary

Introduces `ToolCallContext` — an immutable, framework-agnostic key-value bag that carries out-of-band metadata (auth tokens, tenant IDs, correlation IDs) through the tool execution pipeline to MCP calls, without exposing it to the LLM.

Resolves Issue #1323

## Context Flow

```
ProcessOptions.toolCallContext
  → DefaultToolLoop (stores, forwards on every call)
    → tool.call(input, context)
      → DelegatingTool chains (auto-propagation)
        → SpringToolCallbackWrapper → Spring AI ToolContext → MCP
        → MethodTool → injects into @LlmTool method parameters
```

## Major Changes

### New: `ToolCallContext`

Immutable typed key-value bag with merge semantics, `EMPTY` singleton, and `toMap()` for Spring AI bridging.

### New: `Tool.call(input, context)` overload

Two-arg call method on `Tool` interface. Default discards context for full backward compatibility.

### Canonical `DelegatingTool` call pattern

`DelegatingTool.call(String)` now routes through `call(String, ToolCallContext.EMPTY)`, making the two-arg method the **single canonical entry point** for decorator logic. All decorators override one method only — `call(String, ToolCallContext)`. ArchUnit test (`DelegatingToolArchitectureTest`) runs on every `mvn test` to enforce this contract.

### Updated: `MethodTool` context injection

`@LlmTool` methods can declare a `ToolCallContext` parameter — framework injects it at call time and **excludes it from the LLM-facing JSON schema**. Works for both Kotlin and Java methods.

### Updated: Spring AI bridges

`SpringToolCallbackAdapter` and `SpringToolCallbackWrapper` convert between `ToolCallContext` and Spring AI `ToolContext` in both directions. `SpringToolCallbackAdapter` deduplicated to a single call path.

### Updated: `ProcessOptions`

New `toolCallContext` property with `withToolCallContext(Map)` Java-friendly overload.

### New: `ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter`

Allowlist/denylist filter controlling which context entries cross the MCP boundary. **Defined but not yet wired** — integration pending Spring AI MCP `_meta` finalization.

## Not Yet Included

- `ToolCallContextMcpMetaConverter` wiring into `SpringToolCallbackWrapper`
- `PromptRunner`-level context enrichment (per-interaction override)
