title: Deep Refactoring of  API createObjectWithThinking
body:
## Overview

 * Align with createObject pattern for consistency
  * Enhance LLMOperations interface and add impl to Abstract LLM Ops
  * Add thinking transformation method into ToolLoopLLmOperations
  * Left Legacy implimentation using spring AI unchanged
  * implemented switch to toggle between modern and legacy code
  * updated unit tests
  
Please refer to issue: https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/1438

  ## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Refactored createObjectWithThinking  to go through the same code path as createObject - with full tool loop support, tool decoration, LlmRequestEvent   publishing, retry/timeout handling, and guardrails validation.                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Key Changes                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Unified code path: Thinking methods now use the same infrastructure as non-thinking methods (tool loop, retries, timeouts, event publishing)                                              
  - ThinkingException wrapping: Conversion errors preserve thinking blocks for debugging                                                                                                      
  - Guardrail no-retry: GuardRailViolationException now fails immediately without retries (policy decisions shouldn't be retried)                                                             
  - Switch pattern: ChatClientLlmOperations.doTransformWithThinking switches between Embabel tool loop and legacy Spring AI path based on useEmbabelToolLoop flag                             
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Changes by File                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Core Implementation                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - LlmOperations.kt - Added 4-param doTransformWithThinking interface method                                                                                                                 
  - AbstractLlmOperations.kt - Implemented createObjectWithThinking with getToolsAndEvent, tool decoration, retry template, and executeWithTimeout                                            
  - ToolLoopLlmOperations.kt - Implemented doTransformWithThinking - extracts thinking from final response, wraps conversion errors in ThinkingException                                      
  - ChatClientLlmOperations.kt - Override with switch pattern: useEmbabelToolLoop to super (tool loop) or doTransformWithThinkingSpringAi (legacy)                                            
  - OperationContextDelegate.kt - Updated createObjectWithThinking to use ProcessContext path instead of direct SPI call                                                                      
  - LlmDataBindingProperties.kt - Added GuardRailViolationException to notRetryOn list                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Tests                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - ToolLoopLlmOperationsTest.kt - Added DoTransformWithThinkingTests nested class (String, structured output, exception handling)                                                            
  - OperationContextDelegateTest.kt - Updated to test new ProcessContext path                                                                                                                 
  - DummyObjectCreatingLlmOperations.kt - Added stub implementations for new interface methods                                                                                                
  - ScriptedLlmOperations.kt - Added stub implementations for new interface methods                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Integration Test Fixes                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - LLMAnthropicThinkingIT.java - Fixed timeout: 240 to 240s                                                                                                                                  
  - LLMOllamaThinkingIT.java - Fixed timeout: 240 to 240s                                                                                                                                     
  - LLMOpenAiGuardRailsIntegrationIT.java - Fixed timeout: 240 to 240s                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Design HighLights - matching Legacy behavior                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  1. Extract thinking from final response only - Matches legacy behavior, thinking blocks from intermediate tool iterations are not captured     \(see not on possible follow up optimization)                                             
  2. String output returns raw text - Not sanitized, thinking tags preserved for caller inspection                                                                                            
  3. Structured output uses converter chain - SuppressThinkingConverter strips thinking before JSON parsing. Thinking  LLM output gets preserved from LLM raw output  prior to using converter.                                                                              
  4. ThinkingException preserves context - When conversion fails, thinking blocks are captured in exception for analysis                                                                     
  5. validateAssistantResponse receives full ThinkingResponse - Guardrails can inspect both result and thinking blocks                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Note on Optimization Opportunity :   Collecting thinking blocks in tool loop callback                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Currently, thinking blocks are extracted only from the final response of the tool loop. An optimization opportunity exists to collect thinking blocks from all iterations via the tool loop 
  callback mechanism.                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Rationale:                                                                                                                                                                                  
  - LLMs may produce valuable reasoning in intermediate tool-calling iterations                                                                              
  - The tool loop already has callback infrastructure that could be extended to accumulate thinking blocks across iterations                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Trade-offs to consider:                                                                                                                                                                     
  - Increased memory usage (accumulating blocks across iterations)                                                                                                                            
  - Potential for duplicate/redundant thinking content                                                                                                                                        
  - May require changes to ToolLoop callback interface                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  _Please advise on whether this optimization should be pursued in a follow-up PR._        
"Over-optimization is evil":)

title: MaybeReturn enhancements
body:
## Overview  -      MaybeReturn Handling for Empty Strings and Malformed JSON         

Superceded PR:        https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/pull/1386                            
                                                                                
  This PR improves the robustness of MaybeReturn<T> handling in                 
  doTransformIfPossible operations by addressing two distinct concerns:     
    
  1. Empty string handling at the outputParser level                            
  2. Malformed JSON handling at the deserializer level                          
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
  ## Part 1: Empty String Handling                                                 
                                                                                
  ### The Problem                                                                   
                                                                                
  When a tool requests replanning during the tool loop, DefaultToolLoop         
  terminates early and passes an empty string to the outputParser:              
   
```                                                                             
  // DefaultToolLoop.kt:153-154                                                 
  logger.info("Tool loop terminated for replan after {} iterations",            
  state.iterations)                                                             
  return buildResult("", outputParser, state)  // Empty string!                 
  ```                                                                            
  OLD Behavior (Bug)                                                            
  Scenario: Replan requested                                                    
  What Happened: outputParser("") → Jackson throws JsonParseException: No       
  content                                                                       
     to map → InvalidLlmReturnFormatException                                   
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Scenario: LLM returns empty                                                   
  What Happened: Same as above                                                  
  **Problem**: The replan case threw a misleading "No content to map" exception     
  instead of properly signaling replan.                                         
                                                                                
  NEW Behavior (Fix)                                                            
  Scenario: Replan requested                                                    
  What Happens: outputParser("") → MaybeReturn.noOutput() → caller checks       
    replanRequested → throws ReplanRequestedException                           
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Scenario: LLM returns empty                                                   
  What Happens: outputParser("") → MaybeReturn.noOutput() →                     
    Result.failure(Exception("No output available"))       
                     
  **Key insight:** From outputParser's perspective, there's no way to distinguish   
  replan vs empty LLM response—both are empty strings. The fix handles both     
  gracefully, and the caller uses replanRequested flag to determine the actual  
  cause.                                                                        
                                                                                
  Implementation                                                                
 ```                                                                               
  // ToolLoopLlmOperations.kt                                                   
  val outputParser: (String) -> MaybeReturn<O> = { text ->                      
      if (text.isNotBlank()) {                                                  
          converter.convert(text)!!                                             
      } else {                                                                  
          MaybeReturn.noOutput()                                                
      }                                                                         
  }                                                                             
                                                                                
  Factory methods added to MaybeReturn:                                         
  companion object {                                                            
      fun <T> noOutput(): MaybeReturn<T> = MaybeReturn(failure = "No output     
  available")                                                                   
      fun <T> failure(message: String): MaybeReturn<T> = MaybeReturn(failure =  
  message)                                                                      
  }                                                                             
  ```                                                                              
  ---                                                                           
 ##  Part 2: Malformed JSON Deserialization                                        
                                                                                
  ### The Problem                                                                   
                                                                                
  LLM responses may contain malformed or edge-case JSON that the standard       
  Jackson deserializer would either crash on or misinterpret.                   
                                                                                
  Solution: Custom MaybeReturnDeserializer                                      
                                                                                
  A custom deserializer that gracefully converts all edge cases into            
  MaybeReturn.failure() with descriptive messages.                              
                                                                                
  Handled Cases                                                                 
                                                                                
  #### Valid Cases                                                                   
  ┌──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐     
  │            Input             │                 Result                 │     
  ├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤     
  │ {"success": <valid_object>}  │ MaybeReturn(success = object)          │     
  ├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤     
  │ {"failure": "error message"} │ MaybeReturn(failure = "error message") │     
  └──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘     
 
#### Edge Cases (all converted to failures)                                        
  Input: {"success": null}                                                      
  Result: failure("Success value was null")                                     
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"failure": null}                                                      
  Result: failure("Failure indicated but no message provided")                  
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": {}} (missing required fields)                              
  Result: failure("Missing required field: <name>")                             
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": <invalid_structure>}                                       
  Result: failure("Invalid data format for expected type")                      
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": X, "failure": Y} (both non-null)                           
  Result: failure("Both success and failure provided")                          
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": null, "failure": null} (both null)                         
  Result: failure("Both success and failure provided")                          
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": X, "failure": null} (one value)                            
  Result: deserialize success (ignore null failure)                             
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"success": null, "failure": "msg"} (one value)                        
  Result: deserialize failure (ignore null success)                             
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"failure": 123} (non-string)                                          
  Result: failure("Failure message must be a string")                           
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"failure": {}} (object/array)                                         
  Result: failure("Failure message must be a string")                           
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {"failure": ""} (blank string)                                         
  Result: failure("Failure message was empty")                                  
  ────────────────────────────────────────                                      
  Input: {} (neither field)                                                     
  Result: failure("Neither success nor failure field provided")                 
  Key Implementation Details                                                    
                                                                                
                                                                              
  #### Note on Empty String                                                          
                                                                                
  Empty string "" is not valid JSON and causes JsonParseException before the    
  deserializer is invoked. Empty string handling is done at the outputParser    
  level (Part 1), not in the deserializer.                                      
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
  Files Changed                                                                 
                                                                                
  - LlmOperationsCommon.kt - Added MaybeReturn factory methods and              
  MaybeReturnDeserializer                                                       
  - ToolLoopLlmOperations.kt - Updated outputParser to handle empty strings     
  - MaybeReturnDeserializerTest.kt - Comprehensive tests for all edge cases     
  - ToolLoopLlmOperationsTest.kt - Enabled replan test                          
  - ChatClientLlmOperationsThinkingTest.kt - Disabled test pending Spring AI    
  thinking refactoring                                                          
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
  Testing                                                                       
                                                                                
  - Unit tests for all deserializer edge cases                                  
  - Replan scenario test enabled and passing                                    
  - Existing tests continue to pass

title: Add event triggers feature
body:
# EventTrigger: system-initiated chatbot actions
                                                                                                                                                      
##  Summary                                         

  Adds EventTrigger — a mechanism for the system to send prompts to the chatbot on behalf of users where only the chatbot's response is visible. The trigger prompt reaches the LLM but is never stored in the conversation.

##  Motivation

  Use cases like welcome greetings, daily briefings, and group notifications require the system to prompt the chatbot on a user's behalf. Previously, these prompts were stored as visible UserMessages in the conversation and also `embabel-chat-store`, cluttering the chat history. An EventTrigger is not a message — it's an event on the agent process blackboard.

##  Changes

  Conversation.kt
  - Added lastMessageIfInRole(vararg roles: MessageRole) — flexible role-based query that returns the last message if its role matches any of the given roles
  - Deprecated lastMessageIfBeFromUser() in favor of lastMessageIfInRole(MessageRole.USER)

  **ChatSession.kt**
  - Added onTrigger(trigger: EventTrigger) with default no-op implementation for subclasses to override

  **AgentProcessChatbot.kt**
  - Implemented onTrigger() in AgentProcessChatSession — adds the trigger to the blackboard and runs the agent process, but does not call conversation.addMessage(). Compare with onUserMessage() which does both.

  **DefaultChatAgentBuilder.kt**
  - Broadened precondition: fires on user messages or triggers (conversation.lastMessageIfInRole(MessageRole.USER) != null || context.lastResult() is EventTrigger)
  - Extracted buildToolGroup(), buildRendering(), templateModel(), and generateResponse() helper methods from the inline transformation
  - generateResponse() dispatches to respondWithTrigger() or respondWithSystemPrompt() based on whether a trigger is present
  - The assistant's response IS stored in the conversation and sent to the output channel — only the trigger prompt is hidden

  **PromptRunner.kt**
  - Added respondWithTrigger() to the Rendering interface — responds to a system-initiated trigger using the rendered template as system prompt

  **DelegatingRendering.kt**
  - Implemented respondWithTrigger() — same as respondWithSystemPrompt() but appends the trigger as a UserMessage in the LLM messages list (not in the
   conversation)

  **PromptRunnerRendering.kt (test support)**
  - Implemented respondWithTrigger() for test PromptRunnerRendering

##  What this enables

  - Welcome greetings: EventTrigger("Greet new user Alice", listOf(alice)) — user sees only the greeting
  - Daily briefings: EventTrigger("Give morning briefing", listOf(subscriber))
  - Group notifications: EventTrigger("Surf is up at North Beach", surfers)

##  What stays the same

  - Regular onUserMessage() path is completely unchanged
  - No changes to StoredConversation, MessageData, or UI/filtering

title: Fix Guide Issue 31 - don't call out for vector dimensions if already …
body:
# Fix startup crash when embedding endpoint is unavailable (guide#31)                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                      
##  Problem                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                      
When running the Embabel Hub with Azure OpenAI, the application crashes at startup with:                                                            
                                                                                                                                                      
NonTransientAiException: 404 - {"error":{"code":"404","message": "Resource not found"}}

The failure occurs because DrivineStore.createVectorIndex calls Spring AI's AbstractEmbeddingModel.dimensions(), which makes a live API call to determine embedding vector dimensions. Azure OpenAI deployments that only expose chat completions (e.g., gpt-4.1_corporate) do not serve the embeddings endpoint, resulting in a 404 that crashes the entire application during bean initialization.

##  Root Cause

SpringAiEmbeddingService.dimensions unconditionally delegates to model.dimensions(), triggering a network call — even though the dimensions are already known from YAML configuration (openai-models.yml / google-genai-models.yml).

##  Fix

  - Add optional configuredDimensions parameter to SpringAiEmbeddingService. When set, the configured value is returned directly, bypassing the live
  API call.
  - Wire the dimensions from YAML model definitions through the OpenAI and Google GenAI autoconfiguration paths.

##  Changes

  ```
┌─────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              File               │                                   Change                                    │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ SpringAiEmbeddingService.kt     │ Add configuredDimensions: Int? parameter; prefer it over model.dimensions() │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ OpenAiCompatibleModelFactory.kt │ Accept and pass through configuredDimensions                                │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ OpenAiModelsConfig.kt           │ Pass embeddingDef.dimensions from YAML config                               │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ GoogleGenAiModelsConfig.kt      │ Pass embeddingDef.dimensions from YAML config                               │
  ├─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ SpringAiEmbeddingServiceTest.kt │ New test: verifies configured dimensions skip API call; verifies fallback   │
  └─────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

##  Notes

  - Backwards compatible: configuredDimensions defaults to null, so providers that don't specify dimensions (Bedrock, Ollama, Docker, LMStudio) are
  unaffected.
  - Also improves startup performance for all users by eliminating an unnecessary network round-trip when dimensions are known from config.

  Fixes https://github.com/embabel/guide/issues/31

title: ToolLoop Callbacks
body:
## ToolLoop Callbacks: Inspectors and Transformers                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                              
 ### Overview                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                              
 Extensible callback system for observing and transforming tool loop execution. Enables logging, metrics, debugging, history compression, and result transformation without modifying core   loop logic.             

* Introduction of ToolLoopCallback Interface APIs
* Simple Callbacks Immplementation for Tool Loop Inspection and Transformation
* Introduced Callbacks SPIs
* Factored SPI callbacks into DefaultToolLoop
* AfterToolResultContext - added result: Tool.Result property
* DefaultToolLoop - executeToolCall returns Pair<Tool.Result, String>                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Architecture                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Two callback types with clear separation of concerns:                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - **`ToolLoopInspector`** - Read-only observers for logging, metrics, debugging                                                                                                             
  - **`ToolLoopTransformer`** - Read-write transformers for history compression, summarization, result modification                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Callback Lifecycle                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  | Hook | Inspector (observe) | Transformer (modify) |                                                                                                                                       
  |------|---------------------|----------------------|                                                                                                                                       
  | Before LLM call | `beforeLlmCall()` | `transformBeforeLlmCall()` → `List<Message>` |                                                                                                      
  | After LLM response | `afterLlmCall()` | `transformAfterLlmCall()` → `Message` |                                                                                                           
  | After tool result | `afterToolResult()` | `transformAfterToolResult()` → `String` |                                                                                                       
  | After iteration | `afterIteration()` | `transformAfterIteration()` → `List<Message>` |                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Context Classes                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  All contexts extend `CallbackContext` base class with common properties:                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                              
```                                                                                                                                                                            
  abstract class CallbackContext(                                                                                                                                                             
      open val history: List<Message>,                                                                                                                                                        
      open val iteration: Int,                                                                                                                                                                
  )     
 
```           

                                                                                                                                                                     
  ┌────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                                                  
  │        Context         │             Additional Properties                                                                                                                │                                                                                                                  
  ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                                                  
  │ BeforeLlmCallContext   │ tools, tokenEstimate                                                                                                                 │                                                                                                                  
  ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                                                  
  │ AfterLlmCallContext    │ response, usage                                                                                                                          │                                                                                                                  
  ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                                                  
  │ AfterToolResultContext │ toolCall, result: Tool.Result, resultAsString                                                                          │                                                                                                                  
  ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                                                  
  │ AfterIterationContext  │ toolCallsInIteration                                                                                                                     │                                                                                                                  
  └────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                                                  

### Built-in Implementations                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ToolLoopLoggingInspector - Configurable logging at DEBUG/INFO/WARN levels                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ToolResultTruncatingTransformer - Truncates large tool results to reduce token usage                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                              
### Usage:
```                                                                                                                                                                                              
  val loggingInspector = ToolLoopLoggingInspector(                                                                                                                                            
      logLevel = ToolLoopLoggingInspector.LogLevel.INFO                                                                                                                                       
  )                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  val truncatingTransformer = ToolResultTruncatingTransformer(                                                                                                                                
      maxLength = 5000,                                                                                                                                                                       
      logLevel = ToolLoopLoggingInspector.LogLevel.INFO                                                                                                                                       
  )                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ai.withDefaultLlm()                                                                                                                                                                         
      .withTools(tools)                                                                                                                                                                       
      .withToolLoopInspectors(loggingInspector)                                                                                                                                               
      .withToolLoopTransformers(truncatingTransformer)                                                                                                                                        
      .creating(MyResult::class.java)                                                                                                                                                         
      .fromPrompt("...")                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Custom Inspector Example                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  val inspector = object : ToolLoopInspector {                                                                                                                                                
      override fun afterToolResult(context: AfterToolResultContext) {                                                                                                                         
          // Access typed result                                                                                                                                                              
          when (context.result) {                                                                                                                                                             
              is Tool.Result.Text -> logger.info("Text result")                                                                                                                               
              is Tool.Result.WithArtifact -> logger.info("Has artifact")                                                                                                                      
              is Tool.Result.Error -> logger.warn("Error: ${context.result.message}")                                                                                                         
          }                                                                                                                                                                                   
      }                                                                                                                                                                                       
  }                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Custom Transformer Example                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  val summarizer = object : ToolLoopTransformer {                                                                                                                                             
      override fun transformAfterIteration(context: AfterIterationContext): List<Message> {                                                                                                   
          if (context.history.size > 20) {                                                                                                                                                    
              return summarizeOlderMessages(context.history)                                                                                                                                  
          }                                                                                                                                                                                   
          return context.history                                                                                                                                                              
      }                                                                                                                                                                                       
  }                                                                                                                                                                                           
   ```
                                                                                                                                                                                           
  #### Parallel Tool Loop Support                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Callbacks work with both sequential DefaultToolLoop and ParallelToolLoop:                                                                                                                   
  - Inspectors notified for each tool result                                                                                                                                                  
  - Transformers applied to results before adding to history                                                                                                                                  
  - Order preserved regardless of parallel execution timing                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  #### Package Structure                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  com.embabel.agent.api.tool.callback/                                                                                                                                                        
  ├── ToolLoopCallback.kt          # Interfaces and context classes                                                                                                                           
  ├── ToolLoopLoggingInspector.kt  # Logging inspector                                                                                                                                        
  └── ToolResultTruncatingTransformer.kt  # Truncation transformer                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ### Implementation Details                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - DefaultToolLoop - executeToolCall() returns Pair<Tool.Result, String> preserving typed result                                                                                             
  - ParallelToolLoop - ParallelToolResult.Success holds both result and resultContent                                                                                                         
  - Factory functions in ToolLoopCallbackSupport.kt for context creation                                                                                                                      
  - Extension functions for applying inspectors/transformers to lists                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
#### Separate Note on OperationContextDelegate

Number of parameters grows, perhaps, requiries planning how mitigate thr growth.

#### Comprehensive Integration Tests Location

```
meta-agent/meta-agent-service/src/test/kotlin/com/embabel/metaagent/service/ToolLoopCallbacksIntegrationTest.kt

```

title: Fixes #532
body:
PR: Capture post-augmentation LLM prompts via InstrumentedChatModel

Problem

ChatModelCallEvent was emitted before the tool loop via emitCallEvent(), so it captured the prompt as Embabel constructed it — missing tool schemas, format instructions, and chat options that Spring AI adds before the actual model call. Debugging prompt visibility required comparing what we logged vs what the model actually received.

Solution

Introduce InstrumentedChatModel, a pure-composition ChatModel decorator that intercepts call(Prompt) at the point Spring AI has finished augmenting the prompt. It emits ChatModelCallEvent with the fully resolved prompt and options, then delegates to the real model.

Integration points

InstrumentedChatModel wraps ChatModel in both execution paths when LlmRequestEvent is present:

  • Tool loop path: ChatClientLlmOperations.createMessageSender() wraps before passing to SpringAiLlmMessageSender
  • ChatClient path: ChatClientLlmOperations.createChatClient() wraps before building ChatClient

The redundant emitCallEvent() override is removed — InstrumentedChatModel now serves as the single authoritative event source.

Design decisions

  • Explicit delegation, not Kotlin by: Java default methods (getDefaultOptions(), stream()) are not delegated by Kotlin's by mechanism — they silently call the interface default. Explicit delegation ensures correctness and makes new ChatModel methods a compile error.
  • No AOP: Domain context (LlmRequestEvent) is captured at construction time. No ThreadLocal, no proxy magic.
  • Fallback path preserved: When llmRequestEvent is null (non-production paths), createMessageSender falls back to the uninstrumented llm.createMessageSender(options).

Files changed

File | Change -- | -- InstrumentedChatModel.kt | New — ChatModel decorator InstrumentedChatModelTest.kt | New — 14 tests ChatClientLlmOperations.kt | Wire instrumentation in createMessageSender; remove emitCallEvent() override ToolLoopLlmOperations.kt | Add llmRequestEvent parameter to createMessageSender ToolLoopLlmOperationsTest.kt | Fix overrides for new createMessageSender signature ChatClientLlmTransformerTest.kt | Event count unchanged (old event replaced, not added) LlmOperationsTest.kt | New — tests for interface default methods

Verified at runtime

Shell -p flag confirms paired events per LLM call: the InstrumentedChatModel event shows resolved OpenAiChatOptions with temperature, streamUsage, etc. — confirming full prompt visibility.

title: Fix: isolate servlet-dependent beans to prevent NoClassDefFoundError
body:
This pull request improves the auto-configuration of observability features in the Embabel Agent by isolating servlet-dependent beans into a nested configuration class. This change prevents class loading issues in non-web applications and ensures servlet-related beans are only created when relevant servlet classes are present and HTTP tracing is enabled.

Key improvements:

**Servlet-dependent bean isolation:**

title: Provide both Kotlin and Java code samples.
Experimental Configurable Feature Parallel Tool Loop
body:
## Summary      

Please refer to issue:
 https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/404                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Adds experimental `ParallelToolLoop` that executes multiple tool calls from a single LLM response concurrently, reducing latency for I/O-bound operations.                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Motivation:** When LLM requests 5 tools (each 2s), sequential = 10s, parallel = 2s.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## New Files                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  | File | Description |                                                                                                                                                                      
  |------|-------------|                                                                                                                                                                      
  | `api/tool/config/ToolLoopConfiguration.kt` | Spring Boot config properties for tool loop (type, timeouts, executor) |                                                                     
  | `spi/loop/ToolLoopFactory.kt` | Factory interface with "hidden" impl, accessed via `ToolLoopFactory.default()` |                                                                            
  | `spi/loop/support/ParallelToolLoop.kt` | Parallel execution using `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync()` with per-tool/batch timeouts |                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Modified Files                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  | File | Changes |                                                                                                                                                                          
  |------|---------|                                                                                                                                                                          
  | `spi/loop/support/DefaultToolLoop.kt` | Added `open class`, extracted `protected open fun processToolCalls()` as extension point |                                                        
  | `spi/support/ToolLoopLlmOperations.kt` | Inject `ToolLoopFactory` with default, use factory to create tool loop |                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Key Design Decisions                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - **Collect-then-add pattern**: Execute in parallel, add results to history in original order                                                                                               
  - **First-wins for replan**: First `ReplanRequestedException` in order stops the loop                                                                                                       
  - **Injection strategy**: Applied once after all tools complete (last tool's context)                                                                                                       
  - **Configuration**: `embabel.agent.platform.toolloop.type=parallel` to enable                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Discussion point                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Refactor DefaultToolLoop to use shared helpers (composition over inheritance) - extract common logic to helper classes instead of protected methods

title: fix: Wrap non-JSON tool responses for Gemini compatibility
body:
https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/1391

###   Summary

  Google GenAI (Gemini) requires tool responses (FunctionResponse.response) to be valid JSON objects. When a tool returns a plain text string, Spring AI's GoogleGenAiChatModel.parseJsonToMap() either:

  1. Crashes with a JsonParseException - for MatryoshkaTool responses that return plain text like "Enabled 4 tools: ..."
  2. Silently drops the content - for RAG/search tools returning plain text results, causing the LLM to hallucinate 

  The same tools work correctly with OpenAI, which accepts plain text in tool response content fields.

###   Root cause

  All tool results flow through messageConverters.kt before being sent to the LLM. The textContent was passed as-is to ToolResponseMessage.ToolResponse.responseData without ensuring it's valid JSON. 

Most tools worked "by luck" because MethodTool.convertResult() serializes non-String return types to JSON via Jackson only tools returning a raw String (or implementing Tool directly like MatryoshkaTool) were affected.

### Fix

  - messageConverters.kt: Added ensureJson() extension function that wraps non-JSON tool response text in {"result": "..."} before sending to the LLM. 
  - JSON objects and arrays are preserved as-is. This acts as a safety net at the single conversion point all tools pass through.
  - MatryoshkaTool.kt: Changed SimpleMatryoshkaTool.call() and SelectableMatryoshkaTool.call() to return structured JSON ({"enabled_tools_count": N, "enabled_tools": [...]}) instead of plain text, via a shared enabledToolsJson() helper.

### Test plan

  - MessageConversionTest: new tests covering plain text wrapping, JSON object/array preservation, and whitespace handling
  - MatryoshkaToolTest: All assertions updated to verify JSON format responses
  - Manual verification with https://github.com/embabel/ragbot + Google GenAI to confirm no more JsonParseException and no hallucination

title: Fix: Merge consecutive ToolResponseMessages for Gemini parallel tool call
body:
## Summary       

https://github.com/embabel/embabel-agent/issues/1383                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - Fix Google Gemini models failing with parallel tool calls (`400: number of function response parts must equal function call parts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Added `mergeConsecutiveToolResponses()` in `messageConverters.kt` to group consecutive `ToolResponseMessage` entries into a single message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  - Applied the merge in `SpringAiLlmMessageSender` after message conversion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  **Root cause:** Each `ToolResultMessage` was converted to a separate `ToolResponseMessage`. Gemini requires all function responses for a single tool-calling turn to be in one message. OpenAI/Anthropic are not affected.                                                                                                                                                         

  ## Changes

  - **`messageConverters.kt`** — Added `mergeConsecutiveToolResponses()` extension function
  - **`SpringAiLlmMessageSender.kt`** — Applied the merge after converting messages
  - **`MessageConversionTest.kt`** — Added 6 unit tests

  ## Open question

  Could this merging behavior cause issues with other existing Embabel tools (e.g. tools that rely on individual `ToolResponseMessage` ordering, or tools with side effects that depend on being processed one at a time)? The merge only affects the Spring AI message layer sent to the LLM provider — tool execution itself is unchanged — but this should be investigated to confirm there are no unexpected interactions with the broader tool ecosystem.

  - [x] New `MergeConsecutiveToolResponsesTests` (6 tests)
  - [x] Existing `SpringAiLlmMessageSenderTest`

## Summary

  ├── Conversation              ← uses User for attribution
  ├── ConversationFactory

title: Fix inconsistent naming of PromptRunner sub-runners
body:
This PR attempts to solve the inconsistencies of the various `PromptRunner` sub-runners (see #1306), both in terms of the name of the factory methods that create them as well as the interface names that are returned by these interfaces.

It solves these inconsistencies by using a gerund form for all factory methods, and using the same name for the interfaces that return them. The sub-runner interfaces are defined within the scope of `PromptRunner` itself, because implementations of these interfaces are only meant to be used within the scope of a `PromptRunner` implementation.

Specifically, the following changes were made:

| Old Factory Method | Old Interface Name | New Factory Method | New Interface Name |
| ---: 	  			 | :---				  | ---:			   | :--- 				|
| `PromptRunner::creating(Class)` | `ObjectCreator<T>` | `PromptRunner::creating(Class)` (identical)| `PromptRunner.Creating<T>` |
| `PromptRunnerOperations::withTemplate(String)` | `TemplateOperations` | `PromptRunner::rendering(String)` | `PromptRunner.Rendering`
| `StreamingPromptRunner::stream()` | `StreamingPromptRunnerOperations` | `StreamingPromptRunner::streaming(Class)` | `StreamingPromptRunner.Streaming`
| `PromptRunner::withThinking()` | `ThinkingPromptRunnerOperations` | `PromptRunner::thinking()` | `PromptRunner.Thinking`|

Note that `PromptRunnerOperations::withTemplate` was moved down to `PromptRunner` for consistency.

The old interfaces and methods have been marked with deprecation notices.

title: Fixes #883
body:
This pull request introduces a more resilient approach for MCP client auto-configuration in the Agent Platform by replacing Spring AI's default configuration with a custom implementation. The changes ensure that MCP client initialization failures no longer prevent application startup, and instead, errors are logged and the application continues to run. The update also introduces a filter to exclude the default Spring AI MCP client auto-configuration and properly registers these changes for Spring Boot's auto-configuration mechanism.

The most important changes are:

**Resilient MCP Client Auto-Configuration:**

* Added `QuiteMcpClientAutoConfiguration`, which extends Spring AI's `McpClientAutoConfiguration` but wraps MCP client initialization in try-catch blocks to prevent startup failures if a client cannot be initialized. Errors are logged and only successfully initialized clients are registered. This applies to both synchronous and asynchronous MCP clients.

**Auto-Configuration Filtering:**

* Introduced `AgentPlatformAutoConfigurationFilter`, an `AutoConfigurationImportFilter` that programmatically excludes Spring AI's default `McpClientAutoConfiguration` from being loaded. This ensures that only the Agent Platform's resilient configuration is used.
* Registered the new filter in `META-INF/spring.factories` so that Spring Boot applies it during the auto-configuration phase.

**Auto-Configuration Registration:**

* Modified `AgentPlatformAutoConfiguration` to import `QuiteMcpClientAutoConfiguration` using `@ImportAutoConfiguration`, ensuring that the resilient configuration is automatically applied as part of the platform's startup.

title: Add the ability to exit the current agentic loop if a tool call requests replanning
body:
Sometimes a tool call made by an LLM may change the state of the blackboard, ideally triggering replanning in light of the new structured data available.  Now we control our own agentic loop, we can support this. The first action will never return, but will have done enough work to inform an advance in the process. In the spirit of Embabel's emphasis on explainability and determinism, there will be a record of what happened.

This is particularly important in chatbots, where routing is a difficult problem. Imagine we're chatting with a user in a general way, no special flow having been invoked. The user says they want to change a reservation, and the chatbot calls the `changeReservation` tool with a given reservation id. At this point we know that we should move to a different state in our flow, and have the structured data in the reservation to explain why. If we can trigger replanning through such  a tool call, we can avoid placing unnecessary routing actions in front of actions that will respond.

The implementation works by introducing `ReplanRequestedException` and letting it propagate up to the current `AgentProcess` implementation to trigger replanning. Replanning excludes the action that was being executed when replanning was triggered to avoid the potential of an infinite loop.

title: Allow nested tools
body:
# Motivation

Tool use is critical to modern Gen AI. Yet an excessive number of tools can consume excessive context space and confuse even good LLMs. Thus tool discovery is an important problem.

This PR addresses this through allowing tools to nest, allowing tool authors to define their tools hierarchically.

This should allow Embabel applications to use any number of tools. As the documentation notes (based on research) it provides the best tool management approach of any framework on any platform.

For example, a single Spotify tool can conceal many playback, search, playlist and other tools. The LLM only has to see the details when it realizes it needs to do something with Spotify.

# Implementation

Introduces nested tools, called **matryoshka** tool after Russian dolls.

A matryoshka tool is the facade that fronts a number of deeper tools. 

Matryoshka tools can be created by implementing the `MatryoshkaTool` subinterface of the `Tool` interface. Convenience methods on the companion make this easy from Java or Kotlin.

Alternatively the `@MatryoshkaTools` annotation on a class containing `LlmTool` annotated methods can expose a top level tool concealing the lower level tools.

title: Migrate internal uses of Spring AI `ToolCallback` to Embabel `Tool` interface and implement our own tool calling loop
body:
# Give Embabel complete control over tool calling

This PR gives Embabel complete control over the tool calling loop within a single LLM interaction. 

Motivations and benefits:

- This will allow support for progressive disclosure of tools, whereby the return of one tool (such as a domain object) can expose additional tools _within the same agentic loop_. This has the potential to bring Embabel's core value of determinism to the implementation of actions, rather than just workflows.
- The ability to support LLM APIs directly if we wish
-Enabling accurate usage to be provided during a single `PromptRunner` invocation. This can be useful to manage cost during a single action. Currently costs are not known until Spring AI returns

## Detailed changes

### Consistently use `Tool` in place of Spring AI `ToolCallback`

Spring AI `ToolCallback` is now used only:

- when we discover MCP tools exposed by Spring AI
- when the user uses the Spring AI `@Tool` annotation instead of Embabel @LlmTool
- in `ChatClientLlmOperations` when we use Spring AI to call a model

### Replace Spring AI tool calling loop with Embabel's own tool loop

We now make a single call at a time to an LLM using the new `LlmMessageSender` interface.

###

Additional tests, not just for new functionality.

## Summary

### API Compatibility Fixes
- Replace custom `ResubscribeTaskRequest` implementation with SDK's `TaskResubscriptionRequest`
- Fix timestamp types from `LocalDateTime` to `OffsetDateTime` per the A2A spec
- Add required null parameter to `AgentSkill` constructor (new parameter in SDK)
- Use `TaskState.isFinal` property instead of manual terminal state check

### A2A Inspector Compatibility Fix
- **Remove message echo in streaming responses** - The A2A 0.3.x clients don't expect `Message` events in the response stream and rejects streams that include them. Removed the echo of the user's message in the streaming response.

## Testing

Tested with the A2A Inspector to verify streaming responses are now accepted correctly.

**Documentation improvements and expanded command references:**

**Architecture and component explanations:**

* The architecture section has been revised to show how auto-configuration and component scanning work together to enable shell commands and services. Key components like `ShellCommands`, `TerminalServices`, and personality providers are described in more detail.

**Human-in-the-loop and chat mode documentation:**

* Expanded sections now describe interactive features such as confirmation prompts, form filling, and goal approval, as well as how to start and operate chat sessions, including log redirection and example interactions.

**Example sessions and best practices:**

* Example command sequences and session walkthroughs are provided to illustrate typical workflows and shell usage, improving onboarding for new users.

title: Fix #1203
body:
This pull request updates the way the `Asyncer` bean is configured in `AsyncConfiguration`. Instead of requiring an `Executor` bean to always be present, it now uses an `ObjectProvider<Executor>` to allow for a fallback executor if none is available. This increases the robustness and flexibility of the bean configuration.

Dependency injection improvement:
